question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI?

options.A: To quickly screen for weight categories and health risks
options.B: To diagnose heart and metabolic diseases directly
options.C: To calculate exact daily food calories
options.D: To measure exact body fat percentage in muscles

explanation: BMI is a quick screening tool to help you spot weight categories that could lead to health issues. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h1)

question: Why is BMI called an indirect measure of body fat?

options.A: It changes based on how much water a person drinks
options.B: It uses overall weight and height instead of direct fat scanning
options.D: It only measures fat right beneath the skin

explanation: Because BMI only uses mass and height proportions, it estimates fat rather than scanning tissue directly. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h1)

question: In the standard metric BMI formula, how is height measured?
explanation: The standard metric formula needs height in meters, which you then square. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h2)

question: When does a nurse use the number 703 in a BMI calculation?

options.A: When adjusting for athletes with high muscle mass
options.B: When the patient's measurements are in pounds and inches
options.C: When the patient is measured in kilograms and meters
options.D: When calculating BMI for an elderly patient

explanation: The number 703 is a handy conversion factor used to balance out imperial units (pounds and inches). Simple as that! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h2)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what BMI value marks the start of the overweight category?
explanation: The overweight category officially starts at a BMI of 25.0 and goes up to 29.9. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h3)

question: A patient has a BMI of 32.5. How is this classified?
explanation: Any BMI value of 30.0 or higher falls under the classification of obesity. Great clinical recall! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h3)

question: Why does a high BMI raise a patient's risk for joint problems like osteoarthritis?

options.A: Extra weight places constant physical stress on weight-bearing joints
options.B: Fat tissue directly destroys cartilage cells
options.C: Obesity causes muscles to shrink completely
options.D: High body weight stops joint fluid from working

explanation: Carrying extra body weight puts constant pressure on weight-bearing joints like the knees and hips, wearing down cartilage over time. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h4)

question: Which health problem is most linked to a very low BMI?
explanation: A low BMI often points to poor nutrition, which weakens bones and lowers the body's immune defenses. You're doing awesome! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h4)

question: Why might a professional athlete be wrongly classified as overweight on a standard BMI chart?

options.A: Their bones are much denser than average
options.B: Their high daily water intake changes the scale
options.C: Their height is usually recorded incorrectly
options.D: Their heavy muscle mass increases total weight without excess fat

explanation: Muscle weighs more than fat by volume! Heavy muscle mass can push an athlete's BMI into the overweight range even with low body fat. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a limitation of using BMI in clinical practice?

options.A: It does not account for changes during pregnancy
options.B: It measures exact fat distribution in the arms
options.C: It can be misleading for elderly patients losing muscle
options.D: It fails to separate muscle weight from fat weight

explanation: BMI doesn't measure fat distribution or target specific body parts like arms; it's just a single ratio of total weight to height. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h5)

question: Why is waist circumference often a better indicator of health risks than BMI?

options.A: It changes based on leg water retention
options.B: It is impossible for athletes to get a false reading
options.D: It specifically measures fat stored around internal abdominal organs

explanation: Waist measurements target belly fat directly, showing the hidden visceral fat around vital organs that drives heart disease risk. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h6)

question: What type of fat does a nurse assess when measuring a patient's waist circumference?
explanation: Waist circumference is our go-to clinical shortcut for checking dangerous visceral fat stored around the tummy and organs. Fantastic finish! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h6)
